# All remaining captured compiler errors: Scape and Run: Parasites backport

Report date: 2026-11-15. Input: recovered SRP 1.10.9 source originally targeting Minecraft 1.12.2. Target: Minecraft 1.7.10 / Forge 10.13.4.1614.

**The complete mod still does not compile and is not playable.** This file includes every one of the **6,683 captured compiler diagnostics across 689 files**, with the full available javac continuation, a matching converted-source location, and a cause explanation or an explicit uncertainty label.

**Count limitation:** javac exited abnormally with code 4. The requested diagnostic limit was 30,000 and was not reached. This is all captured output, not a guaranteed inventory of every defect. Diagnostics are not independent bugs, and their count is not a completion percentage. Some are cascades from a missing superclass/type.

<a id="major-problems"></a>

## Major problems and why they remain

1. **Shared entity behavior and AI:** remaining spawn integration, hands/equipment, movement/navigation and retaliation recruitment still use incompatible platform contracts. EntityParasiteBase alone has 98 diagnostics; failures here cascade into many mobs. No complete original SRP mob has been validated end to end.
2. **Client rendering and particles:** modern renderer, vertex, layer and particle contracts still require native implementations and client checks. The tested shared render-state adapter does not complete these renderers.
3. **Specialized blocks and world generation:** shared block-state plumbing exists, but vanilla codecs, specialized inheritance/callbacks, biomes and structures remain incomplete.
4. **Effects, inventories and persistence:** owning-player HUD visibility, potion items/types/brewing, missing effects, modern stack rules, capabilities, tile/world saved data and progression still need their original behavior preserved across save/reload and multiplayer. Stable effect IDs and server particle visibility have separate passing native tests.
5. **Recovered source and API cascades:** missing types cause secondary symbol/override/generic errors. Recovered syntax and casts also need exact source/bytecode review; adding names alone will not establish correct behavior.
6. **Build and gameplay validation:** the abnormal compiler exit is unresolved. A complete compile, reobfuscated JAR, original-content registration, fresh-world startup, restart, client and multiplayer checks are still required. Passing isolated compatibility tests is insufficient.

Already implemented work includes 51 compatibility source units, narrow access rules, entity query/position boundaries, typed entity synchronization, geometry/state adapters, local difficulty, the native spawn boundary, stable potion IDs, native accepted-application/finish hooks, persisted particle visibility, native armor/toughness and equipment-modifier/damage boundaries, real client tracker synchronization and part of native registration. Recorded verification: 148 compatibility/native groups plus 3 diagnostic-parser/source-snapshot regression tests. All 1,094 original source units and 4,501 original assets are retained. See ARMOR_PORT.md for the latest implementation and test limits. Private-access diagnostics in this snapshot: zero.

The converted sources may still retain a CFR header. That header is provenance, not evidence that the file is the untouched 1.12 reference. This report checks the actual converted files and hashes. Do not match its line numbers against preserved original-source files.

Suggested sequence: stabilize the full compiler run; port remaining entity spawn/AI/equipment/effects; validate one original mob through registration, spawn, AI, damage, save/reload and synchronization; continue client rendering, specialized blocks and world/persistence integration; finally build and validate the complete mod.

<a id="r02"></a>

### R02: Hands, equipment and item-use results

Reported diagnostics: 368.

Why: Modern hand/equipment enums and action-result contracts differ from the single-held-item and slot-based native API.

Required work: Map supported hand/slot behavior and item-use outcomes explicitly; preserve original interaction and equipment semantics.

<a id="r03"></a>

### R03: Movement controllers and movement modes

Reported diagnostics: 216.

Why: Modern movement modes, controller actions and gravity controls differ from the old movement API.

Required work: Implement the required controller state transitions and movement behavior, then validate collision and motion on a real server.

<a id="r04"></a>

### R04: Retaliation AI constructor and recruitment

Reported diagnostics: 125.

Why: The native EntityAIHurtByTarget constructor lacks the modern Class... helper-exclusion argument.

Required work: Preserve exclusion filtering, recruitment bounds and tame-owner behavior in a real AI adapter. Dropping the third argument loses behavior.

<a id="r05"></a>

### R05: AI, path navigation and entity lifecycle

Reported diagnostics: 85.

Why: Entity AI classes, navigation inheritance and lifecycle methods have changed or moved.

Required work: Port the actual targeting, navigation and lifecycle behavior. Climbing/flying/swimming navigation requires more than an empty renamed class.

<a id="r06"></a>

### R06: Potion arguments and numeric effect APIs

Reported diagnostics: 4.

Why: The native potion API uses numeric IDs at constructors and several effect methods, while modern calls often pass Potion objects. The exact receiver and operation determine the fix.

Required work: Constructor conversion and server particle visibility are tested. Inspect the remaining named native operation (for example removePotionEffect), adapt its numeric ID contract, and preserve native gameplay and the implemented visibility lifecycle.

<a id="r07"></a>

### R07: Potion catalogs, types and brewing

Reported diagnostics: 158.

Why: Modern potion catalogs, PotionType and brewing registrations differ from the old effect-ID system.

Required work: Map each vanilla effect and implement potion-type/brewing behavior against native registries without losing recipes or effect data.

<a id="r08"></a>

### R08: Client rendering, particles and model APIs

Reported diagnostics: 460.

Why: The 1.12 rendering/particle pipeline has incompatible classes, generic renderer contracts and member signatures.

Required work: Port particles, vertex submission, models and render layers to the 1.7 client. The verified shared GL-state adapter does not complete the original renderers.

<a id="r09"></a>

### R09: Sound catalogs, categories and packets

Reported diagnostics: 286.

Why: Modern sound constants, category packages, packets and playback signatures do not line up with the native string-based API.

Required work: Use the preserved sound identifiers and native playback/networking at each boundary; verify category and positional behavior. Original custom sound callbacks are already partly converted.

<a id="r10"></a>

### R10: Block states and specialized block APIs

Reported diagnostics: 253.

Why: Modern block rendering, specialized subclasses and state-aware callback contracts differ from native metadata blocks.

Required work: Complete vanilla state codecs and specialized inheritance/callback adapters. The existing state graph and metadata bridge cover only part of this system.

<a id="r11"></a>

### R11: Biomes, world generation and structures

Reported diagnostics: 190.

Why: Modern biome/world-generation types, chunk builders and structure-template APIs differ from the old native interfaces.

Required work: Port biome registration, terrain/structure generation and world queries while preserving the original data and generation rules.

<a id="r12"></a>

### R12: Forge registries and event subscription

Reported diagnostics: 154.

Why: Modern Forge registry-entry/builders and automatic subscriber contracts are absent or incompatible in this target.

Required work: Finish explicit native lifecycle registration and event hookup. Existing item/block registration work does not cover every remaining registry or subscriber.

<a id="r13"></a>

### R13: Advancements and progression

Reported diagnostics: 28.

Why: Minecraft 1.7.10 has no native advancement system matching the imported 1.12 classes.

Required work: Port triggers, persistent completion data and required feedback. Removing triggers or adding no-op stubs would lose progression behavior.

<a id="r14"></a>

### R14: Capabilities and inventory providers

Reported diagnostics: 47.

Why: Modern Forge capabilities and item-handler contracts do not exist in the same form in Forge 1.7.10.

Required work: Implement the actual provider, inventory, serialization and interaction behavior using native hooks, including save/reload and multiplayer validation.

<a id="r15"></a>

### R15: Boss bars and tracking

Reported diagnostics: 70.

Why: The modern tracked BossInfo/BossInfoServer model differs from the old global BossStatus display.

Required work: Port server tracking, progress/state packets and the client HUD. A single global bar or removal of the bar does not preserve the original system.

<a id="r16"></a>

### R16: ItemStack and modern item APIs

Reported diagnostics: 201.

Why: Modern empty-stack, count, property-override and cooldown contracts differ from native nullable stack/item conventions.

Required work: Adapt each stack/item boundary, including empty/null handling, quantities and use behavior; verify the receiver type before rewriting.

<a id="r17"></a>

### R17: Native Vec3 and modern Vec3d boundary

Reported diagnostics: 37.

Why: A native API returns Vec3 where converted code expects the existing Vec3d compatibility type.

Required work: Convert vectors at the native boundary. A global Vec3d-to-Vec3 rename would undo already-tested modern vector semantics.

<a id="r18"></a>

### R18: Raw collections and recovered generic types

Reported diagnostics: 210.

Why: Native APIs or recovered declarations expose raw/Object types where this expression expects a specific generic type.

Required work: Identify the actual collection element type and use a typed boundary or correct declaration. Many entity queries are already migrated; inspect remaining receivers.

<a id="r19"></a>

### R19: Integer-to-byte narrowing

Reported diagnostics: 105.

Why: The expression supplies an int where Java requires a byte; the compiler cannot assume the value fits.

Required work: Inspect the field/key/metadata type and original bytecode before narrowing. Blind casts can truncate values or conceal an incorrectly typed expression.

<a id="r20"></a>

### R20: Fall-damage multiplier

Reported diagnostics: 23.

Why: The native fall method takes one distance argument, whereas this call also passes a damage multiplier.

Required work: Preserve the modern damage calculation and rounding. Dropping the multiplier or simply scaling distance changes damage thresholds.

<a id="r21"></a>

### R21: Entity position method mismatch

Reported diagnostics: 3.

Why: The modern zero-argument block-position call does not match native getPosition(float), which is an interpolated vector method.

Required work: Use the existing EntityQueries.position conversion with floor(x), floor(y + 0.5), floor(z), checking the exact receiver first.

<a id="r22"></a>

### R22: Additional math helpers

Reported diagnostics: 67.

Why: This named modern math helper is unavailable on the target math class.

Required work: Add or route to a behavior-matched implementation and verify edge cases and precision against the original behavior.

<a id="r23"></a>

### R23: GUI, tooltips and chat contracts

Reported diagnostics: 153.

Why: Client GUI/tooltips/chat method signatures and supporting interfaces differ across these Minecraft versions.

Required work: Adapt the real argument and text/rendering contracts. Preserve formatting and behavior rather than discarding extra parameters indiscriminately.

<a id="r24"></a>

### R24: Tile entities, NBT and saved world data

Reported diagnostics: 206.

Why: The named persistence/tile contract is unresolved; it may be a package/signature change or a cascade from an unresolved superclass.

Required work: Check the declared owner and superclass, then port coordinates, dirty marking, ticking, NBT and update packets as needed. Do not assume markDirty itself is universally absent.

<a id="r25"></a>

### R25: Forge event contracts

Reported diagnostics: 10.

Why: Modern event classes, payloads or lifecycle stages differ from those exposed by the target Forge.

Required work: Map each event to the appropriate native hook and preserve ordering, cancellation and client/server side behavior.

<a id="r27"></a>

### R27: Multipart entities

Reported diagnostics: 8.

Why: The multipart entity type or its damage/ownership contract differs from the native target.

Required work: Port entity-part ownership, collision, damage forwarding and required tracking behavior.

<a id="r28"></a>

### R28: Area-effect clouds

Reported diagnostics: 18.

Why: The modern area-effect-cloud entity is not provided by this native version.

Required work: Implement its lifetime, radius, effect application and synchronization behavior or a validated equivalent.

<a id="r29"></a>

### R29: Fluid integration

Reported diagnostics: 1.

Why: The diagnostic occurs in the fluid package, whose original fluid/block integration still needs conversion; this classification alone is not an exact diagnosis.

Required work: Inspect the reported symbol and receiver and port its real fluid/container/rendering boundary. Do not infer a fix from package location alone.

<a id="r30"></a>

### R30: Inheritance, overrides and visibility contracts

Reported diagnostics: 219.

Why: The reported override, generic base-class or visibility contract does not match the target superclass/interface.

Required work: Resolve the actual target signature and superclass first; some errors are cascades from another missing type. Preserve the callback behavior.

<a id="r31"></a>

### R31: Recovered Java syntax, casts and overloads

Reported diagnostics: 26.

Why: Javac rejected the syntax, cast or overload typing of this expression; recovered source and earlier API mismatches can both contribute.

Required work: Compare this exact converted expression with the preserved reference and original bytecode. Fix the verified expression without broad blind substitutions.

<a id="r99"></a>

### R99: Exact root cause still needs individual review

Reported diagnostics: 2952.

Why: The available diagnostic is insufficient for a trustworthy specific root-cause classification. Missing symbols can also cascade from an unresolved parent or incompatible receiver.

Required work: Inspect the exact source line, symbol/location, owner, inheritance and native API. Resolve shared root causes, recompile, and reassess this diagnostic; no specific replacement is asserted here.
